data.narrative:
RoboTwin is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Megi Mejdrechová, Ladislav Dvořák, and David Polák. The company has raised €2.3M in EIC funding to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader comp universe of nine private peers in Robotics & Manufacturing (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI) and one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ), though a narrow same-stage peer set proved insufficient for reliable median-based triangulation.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable here, using the €2.3M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a standard 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression in this sector. This implies a valuation of approximately €5.75M ($6M). Peer-Median valuation was not applied: while ten robotics peers exist in the broader dataset, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables yielded fewer than three datapoints—insufficient for reliable triangulation without introducing sector-wide median bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €4.9M to €6.6M ($5M–$7M), with a median of €5.75M ($6M). This range reflects the mechanical step-up from capital deployed rather than market-derived multiples. Key uncertainties include limited comparable data at the seed stage in this sector and the absence of revenue or product-stage benchmarks. The valuation remains highly sensitive to stage transition assumptions and early commercial traction.
